_comment: Trap catalog. Cells reference these by id via the cell's trap_id field (placed in the map editor's Cell Inspector). trap_type picks the resolution branch: 'damage' rolls damage_range against the victim(s); 'effect' applies the effects.json record in `effect` (damage traps may ALSO carry an effect — it rides along on a failed save); 'teleport' moves the party to params.teleport {map_id, col, row}. params.targets: 'one' (random alive member, default) or 'all'. params.save_stat + params.save_dc give victims a d20 + stat-modifier save — pass = half damage and no effect. params.detect_dc sets the DC of the Detect Traps INT save that spots the trap when it comes into view (default 12). Legacy boolean trap cells (and procedural dungeon traps) resolve to 'dart_trap'. fx_id names the fx.json effect played when the trap goes off (projectile visuals fly in from a nearby wall; teleport traps play it from the trap to where the party lands); empty = a plain burst coloured by damage_type.

traps.name: Dart Trap
traps.description: A spring-loaded dart fires from a hidden housing. The default trap — legacy trap cells and procedural dungeon traps resolve to this record.

traps.name: Fire Trap
traps.description: A glyph of searing flame that engulfs the whole party when tripped.

traps.name: Teleport Trap
traps.description: A translocation glyph that hurls the party elsewhere. Sample record — point params.teleport at your module's destination cell.
